question: Should the law give every worker a four-day week on full pay?
answer: The best evidence now has a comparison group: across 141 organisations and about 2,900 workers, burnout, job satisfaction and health improved after the switch, and not in control firms. Few employers dare cut hours alone, fearing they will look less committed, so a legal default spreads the gain, as the forty-hour week once did.
move: It turns on whether firms that never volunteered would gain as much.
counterpoint: That study's control group was just 12 companies, every firm chose to take part, and hours fell by about five a week, not eight. Nurses, drivers and care workers cannot squeeze a week of shifts into four days: covering the same hours needs 25% more staff. A law would send that bill to hospitals and councils.
source: Fan et al., Nature Human Behaviour, 2025
